```{r}
library(ggplot2)
install.packages("gridExtra")   # install the package
library(gridExtra)
setwd("C:/Users/louis/Downloads/")
df <- read.csv("hotel_sample_5000(4).csv", header=T)
print(df)
summary(df)
sapply(df, function(x) length(unique(x[!is.na(x)])))
colSums(is.na(df))
sum(duplicated(df))
df$country <- factor(df$country)

colnames(df)


```


```{r}
set.seed(2004)

df$canceled <- as.factor(df$canceled)
df$rroom_type <- as.factor(df$rroom_type)
df$market_seg <- as.factor(df$market_seg)
df$deposit_type <- as.factor(df$deposit_type)
df$assroom_type <- as.factor(df$assroom_type)
training <- sample(1:nrow(df), round(2*nrow(df)/3))
library(rpart)



p1 <- rpart(canceled ~ lead_time + weekend_nights + week_nights + adults +
              children + babies + meal + market_seg + channel +
              repeated + pre_cancel + pre_bcn + rroom_type + assroom_type +
              changes + deposit_type + agent + days_wait + customer_type +
              adr + rcar_parking_spaces + ts_requests,
            data = df[training,],
            method = "class",
            parms = list(split = "gini"))
plot(p1)
text(p1, use.n = TRUE, cex = 0.7)
p1_train <- predict(p1, df[training,])
p1p <- ifelse(p1_train[,2] >= 0.5, 1, 0)
t1 <- table(df$canceled[training], p1p)
t1
( t1[1,1] + t1[2,2] ) / sum(t1)
p1_test <- predict(p1, df[-training,])
p1t <- ifelse(p1_test[,2] >= 0.5, 1, 0)
t2 <- table(df$canceled[-training], p1t)
t2
( t2[1,1] + t2[2,2] ) / sum(t2)
```

```{r}

r1 <- rpart(adr ~ lead_time + weekend_nights + week_nights + adults +
              children + babies + meal + market_seg + channel +
              repeated + pre_cancel + pre_bcn + rroom_type + assroom_type +
              changes + deposit_type + agent + days_wait + customer_type +
              rcar_parking_spaces + ts_requests,
            data = df[training,],
            method = "anova")
plot(r1)
text(r1, use.n = TRUE)
r1_pred <- predict(r1, df[-training,])
head(r1_pred)

# True values
y_true <- df$adr[-training]
# Predictions
y_pred <- r1_pred

# Mean Squared Error
MSE <- mean((y_true - y_pred)^2)

# Root Mean Squared Error
RMSE <- sqrt(MSE)

# Mean Absolute Errorq
MAE <- mean(abs(y_true - y_pred))

MSE
RMSE
MAE
```

```{r}
library(randomForest)
train_data <- df[training, ]     # training data
test_data  <- df[-training, ]    # remaining data for testing
train_data$canceled <- as.factor(train_data$canceled)
test_data$canceled  <- as.factor(test_data$canceled)

# Random Forest Classification for 'canceled'
rf_class <- randomForest(canceled ~ lead_time + weekend_nights + week_nights + adults +
                     children + babies + meal + market_seg + channel +
                     repeated + pre_cancel + pre_bcn + rroom_type + assroom_type +
                     changes + deposit_type + days_wait + customer_type +
                     adr + rcar_parking_spaces + ts_requests,
                     data = train_data,
                         ntree = 500,        # Changed from 'num.trees' to 'ntree'
                         importance = TRUE,  # Changed from 'impurity' to TRUE
                         # probability = TRUE is not needed here; 
                         # it calculates probs automatically for factors
                         )

# 3. Check the results
print(rf_class)

# Random Forest Regression for 'adr' (if you still want regression)
rf_reg <- randomForest(adr ~ lead_time + weekend_nights + week_nights + adults +
                   children + babies + meal + market_seg + channel +
                   repeated + pre_cancel + pre_bcn + rroom_type + assroom_type +
                   changes + deposit_type + days_wait + customer_type +
                   rcar_parking_spaces + ts_requests,
                 data = train_data,
                 ntree = 500,
                 importance = TRUE)

# View the model

print(rf_class)

# Predictions

pred_class <- predict(rf_class, test_data)

# Confusion matrix

table(test_data$canceled, pred_class)

# Accuracy

mean(pred_class == test_data$canceled)

# View the model

print(rf_reg)

# Predictions

pred_reg <- predict(rf_reg, test_data)

# Evaluation metrics

MSE <- mean((test_data$adr - pred_reg)^2)
RMSE <- sqrt(MSE)
MAE <- mean(abs(test_data$adr - pred_reg))

MSE
RMSE
MAE

```

```{r}
# --- Visualizing Feature Importance ---

# 1. For the Classification Model (Cancellations)
print("Importance for Cancellation Model:")
varImpPlot(rf_class, main = "Variable Importance - Canceled")


# 2. For the Regression Model (ADR/Price)
print("Importance for ADR Model:")
varImpPlot(rf_reg, main = "Variable Importance - ADR")

```


```{r}

# --- PRUNING THE CLASSIFICATION TREE (p1) ---

# 1. Visualize the Cross-Validation results to see where error is lowest
printcp(p1)   # Prints the table
plotcp(p1)    # Plots the error vs tree size

# 2. Automatically select the best CP (lowest xerror)
best_cp_p1 <- p1$cptable[which.min(p1$cptable[,"xerror"]), "CP"]
print(paste("Best CP for p1 is:", best_cp_p1))

# 3. Prune the tree using that CP
p1_pruned <- prune(p1, cp = best_cp_p1)

# 4. Plot the new, pruned tree
# using rpart.plot is better, but here is the standard plot you used:
plot(p1_pruned, main = "Pruned Classification Tree (Canceled)")
text(p1_pruned, use.n = TRUE, cex = 0.7)

# 5. Check accuracy of the PRUNED tree on Test Data
p1_pruned_pred <- predict(p1_pruned, df[-training,], type = "class") # type="class" gives 0/1 directly
t_pruned <- table(Predicted = p1_pruned_pred, Actual = df$canceled[-training])
print(t_pruned)

# Calculate Accuracy
accuracy_p1 <- sum(diag(t_pruned)) / sum(t_pruned)
print(paste("Accuracy of Pruned Tree:", accuracy_p1))

# --- PRUNING THE REGRESSION TREE (r1) ---

# 1. Visualize results
printcp(r1)
plotcp(r1)

# 2. Automatically select the best CP
best_cp_r1 <- r1$cptable[which.min(r1$cptable[,"xerror"]), "CP"]
print(paste("Best CP for r1 is:", best_cp_r1))

# 3. Prune the tree
r1_pruned <- prune(r1, cp = best_cp_r1)

# 4. Plot the pruned tree
plot(r1_pruned, main = "Pruned Regression Tree (ADR)")
text(r1_pruned, use.n = TRUE, cex = 0.7)

# 5. Check Error (RMSE) of the PRUNED tree
r1_pruned_pred <- predict(r1_pruned, df[-training,])
RMSE_pruned <- sqrt(mean((df$adr[-training] - r1_pruned_pred)^2))

print(paste("RMSE of Pruned Tree:", RMSE_pruned))
```
